eval.per_step_note: scored steps 0..7. The npz carries 10 predicted steps, but val_anchors' gt is capped at K=8, so the tail is NOT scorable from the gt column directly -- do not read this as 'no re-run needed'. gr00t-n15's scripts/kslope_table.py recovers it instead by chaining stride-5 anchors (frame f+k from anchor i+m, step k-5m; costs the last anchor of each episode, 1357/1397), which needs no re-run AND leaves val_anchors byte-identical.

action_parameterization.model_internal_arm_space: delta vs state@t -- see norm_stats action joint means ~0 against state means ~103; converted by model_transforms.outputs -> AbsoluteActions(7 delta + 1 abs)
action_parameterization.gated_at_produce_time: predict_openpi.py refuses to write if subtracting state@t does not shrink the arm chunk (raw-delta output would sit ~38 deg from state instead of ~1.3)
action_parameterization.scoring_note: this label does NOT split the board into competing families. Every row is scored against the same absolute val_anchors gt, and MAE is invariant to a shift both pred and gt share, so a stack that emitted deltas and added them back scores identically either way. The label matters for comparing absolute QUANTITIES across stacks, not for the ranking.

verdict: beats the do-nothing pass line by +1.807 MAE (+58.8%)

determinism.noise: normal(fold_in(key(noise_seed), global_anchor_index)) passed explicitly to policy.infer(noise=...) -- NOT the Policy's internal rng, which splits per call and would make a row depend on iteration order
determinism.reproducibility_note: openpi/JAX is bit-reproducible within a process but not across processes (XLA picks kernels per process). Elementwise this is ~1e-02 deg; on the AGGREGATE it cancels to 7.7e-05 MAE, which is 0.01x this leg's own sampling std (6.7e-03) and ~1000x smaller than the smallest board gap (0.067). So the leaderboard ordering is unaffected, but do NOT expect a re-run to reproduce this npz byte-for-byte, and do not use bit-equality as an integrity check on these files.
